alex.k: Quick RFC follow-up — we still need to pick an approach for the continuous batcher scheduler. do we go lane-based (small/large sequence lanes) or a single priority queue with token-aware batching?

liam: Lane-based seems simpler to reason about for p95 targets. separate queues avoid head-of-line blocking from long sequences. but complexity rises with more lanes. :thinking:

sophia: Agree on HOL blocking concern. our staging runs showed long requests can stall many small batches if mixed. But lanes can starve each other unless we implement cross-lane admission.

arjun: Data point from perf harness: when we introduced naive lane split (50/50 tokens) p95 for short seqs improved ~18ms, but overall throughput dropped ~4% because of underfilled large-lane batches.

jen: If we do lanes we should make them token-aware and let weights be dynamic. e.g., small-lane gets stricter latency budget, large-lane gets opportunistic packing.

liam: Sketch of quick config idea:
```
lane_config:
  - name: small
    max_seq: 128
    weight: 0.7
    batch_timeout_ms: 8
  - name: large
    max_seq: 4096
    weight: 0.3
    batch_timeout_ms: 24
```
This keeps smalls fast but allows long to pack.

alex.k: Two big tradeoffs I want us to capture in the RFC follow-up doc: fairness/admission vs. unit-cost efficiency (tokens per second), and implementation complexity vs. observability.

sophia: Another nuance: preemption. Should small requests be allowed to preempt queued large batches mid-assembly? preemptive cancellation reduces small p95 but increases kernel churn.

arjun: We measured preemption impact: preempting one large batch to fit 4 small requests cost ~0.6ms extra per small request but introduced ~1.2% extra GPU kernel launches in the 1h test. Net latency win but slightly worse GPU efficiency.

jen: +1 on making preemption configurable per lane. Maybe default to non-preemptive and enable preemption only if small p95 exceeds target.

liam: Also think about admission control at RPC layer: reject-or-defer requests when queue depth or token backlog is above threshold. simpler than many lanes for initial rollout.

alex.k: Good idea. admission control buys us headroom while we iterate on lanes. what metrics would drive reject thresholds?

sophia: token_backlog (sum of seq_len in queue), inflight_kv_cache_usage, and p95 delta from baseline.

arjun: Add a short-circuit: if token_backlog > N * gpu_batch_capacity then return 503 w/ Retry-After and a hint for clients to reduce batch size. helps tail latency and avoids meltdown.

jen: Implementation notes for ops: need route-level config in our control plane so customers can set latency vs cost preference. e.g., "latency_mode: strict|balanced|throughput" mapped to lane weights + preemption policy.

liam: Observability: we must emit per-lane metrics: queue_length, token_backlog, average_batch_fill, preemptions, rejected_requests. dashboards for per-route SLO correlations.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rolled scheduler-v2 to staging (tag: sched-v2-canary).

jen: saw the canary. running load now. no obvious errors in logs.

arjun: initial canary results: small p95 -20ms, throughput -6% as earlier. attaching more detailed numbers to RFC doc.

alex.k: Proposed short-term plan (next week):
- implement admission control + opaque priority lane (small/large) with static weights
- add per-lane metrics and a simple control-plane flag per route
- run 24h staging soak and perf harness for typical PLG traffic and enterprise queries

Proposed medium-term (quarter):
- dynamic lane weights based on moving-window p95 and token_backlog
- optional preemption toggle and cost accounting for extra kernel churn
- client-side retry hints for 503s (Retry-After semantics)

Long-term: token-aware compaction, cross-GPU packing, and tighter integration with routing policy for fallback to cheaper model variants under load.

sophia: Action items: @jen add admission control prototype + metrics PR, @arjun run perf harness and attach csv, I'll update the RFC section on fairness models.

jen: i'll get the PR by EOD tomorrow.

arjun: will schedule the 24h soak starting Friday.

liam: can we add a tiny experiment: single-queue + token-aware priority function (score = seq_len * alpha + waiting_time * beta) as baseline? If its within 3% throughput of lanes, prefer simpler.

alex.k: yes, run that as a control. want data before we lock in design.

sophia: Also note edge-case: batched tool-calls with function outputs can change sequence length mid-processing. we need to reserve kv-cache tokens in admission backlog accounting.

jen: noted. will include kv-cache reservation in the prototype.

arjun: scheduling sync Wed 10am to go over results.

liam: thanks all. excited to get concrete numbers. :rocket:

alex.k: thanks team — I'll update the RFC with the plan and link the perf artifacts. filing a follow-up PR after the canary soak. :thumbsup:
